locators: p7 People: Srikhetra Maharana and Kumudini Maharana
supported_claims: The documentation names Srikhetra Maharana and Kumudini Maharana as makers of non-theatrical masks without eye/nose cut-outs.
Its pulp account combines soaked paper,waste cloth and natural fibres with tamarind-seed gum, shaped over a die or sample mask and sun-dried.
Its Cowdung section describes reinforcement over the paper body, shaping facial features while wet, then drying and a chalk-powder/tamarind-gum coating.
limits: Do not treat all Raghurajpur masks as non-theatrical or say no paper mask is worn.
Paper and cow-dung are not necessarily mutually exclusive mask categories: this account layers them in one object.
The p13photograph visibly shows a printed-paper shell beneath added material. Do not infer every photographed stage is beaten pulp or reconcile text/photo by inventing unseen steps.
Do not generalize the source's gender division, termiticidal claim, sacredness rationale, prices, initial-only iconography or market demand.
Use names from text; the p7male portrait is captioned Srikhetra Maharana's son, not Srikhetra himself.

locators: pp13–14 illustrated moulding sequence, explicitly toy body
supported_claims: The p11mask account describes newspaper strips adhered around a mould, complete drying before paint, and a white coating/smoothing stage before coloured finish.
It describes layered paper rather than requiring all paper to be pulped.
Its p23product photograph is captioned an animal-face mask; no performance or wearer is shown.
limits: The illustrated making sequence pp13onward largely demonstrates a bird/toy body with joined halves and a tail. Do not relabel it a step-by-step mask construction sequence.
Exclude broad origin/industrial history and conservation passages: they are not adequate local historical evidence.
Its paste-strength wording is internally inconsistent. Omit chemical/strength/temperature/ratio claims and practical recipe instructions.
Side-ties in p11do not prove theatrical use or identify a named performance.
Do not merge this account with Gambhir's pulp/cow-dung description into a supposedly universal recipe.

locators: Printed p122, PDF p123: Regional Centre, Bhubaneswar; Papier Mache Workshop (Village outreach programme)
supported_claims: The regional centre reports a papier-mâché workshop at Pratisruti in Padanpur, via Jatni, Khordha, on 25–26 July 2016.
It lists Sulachana Maharana and Pratima Maharana of Raghurajpur, Puri, as the demonstrating artists.
Their stated audience was village women and schoolchildren; the report says they demonstrated the process and technique of papier-mâché.
limits: The institutional report spells the village Padanpur; the newspaper spells it Padampur. Prefer the institutional spelling with attribution, without silently asserting the variants are formally equivalent.
The workshop heading says papier-mâché, not specifically masks; do not claim every demonstration or participant object was a mask based on this page alone.
Exclude the report's self-assessment of success and any lasting livelihood, income or present-day training claims.
This corroborates the same reported July 2016 workshop; do not count it as a separate event from NIE.

locators: Opening workshop report, regular page lines46–49
supported_claims: The report describes a two-day Padampur,Khurda mask-making workshop organized by Lalit Kala Akademi's regional centre with Pratisruti, taught by Raghurajpur artists Sulachana Maharana and Pratima Maharana.
Pratima describes newspaper pulp,adhesive and clay moulds,followed by drying,coating and painting; this is attributed maker testimony, not our observation.
The report identifies collection/gifting as uses and distinguishes them from a separate wooden-mask theatre discussion.
limits: Event date is only earlier that week in this article; do not invent exact days.
Do not repeat sweeping every-family claims, productivity, earnings, prices, demand or universal gender roles as current facts.
No statement that training produced lasting income, that every participant continued or that current workshops are available.
No direct quotation planned; do not copy its narrative arrangement.
